Start with what you know and what you want to change.

A short enquiry is enough to begin. If you have a recent bill and a photo of your switchboard, that speeds everything up — but neither is required for a first conversation.

Preparing your enquiry

What makes a first response accurate.

You do not need any of this to get in touch — a rough description is enough to start. But the more of it you can share, the closer the first conversation gets to a real design.

Your approximate consumption

A recent bill is ideal — the quarterly dollar figure is enough. If you know your annual kilowatt hours from a bill or an app, even better: sizing decisions are made in kilowatt hours, not dollars.

Your roof, in plain words

Tiles or metal, roughly how much of it is in sun through the day, and anything that shades it — trees, neighbouring buildings, chimneys. A phone photo from ground level answers most of this at once.

Existing equipment

An older solar array, the inverter's make and model, a battery, an EV charger, a heat pump. Photos of the switchboard and any existing inverter label are the single most useful attachments.

What you want to change

Lower bills, protection from outages, readiness for an electric car, or simply knowing whether the roof is suitable. The goal shapes which design questions get asked first.

Plans for the next few years

An EV, a pool, a heat pump, a renovation, a move. Systems sized around future loads are cheaper to extend later than systems that have to be replaced.

Your location and network

A postcode or suburb is enough. It determines your weather zone, tariffs, network connection rules and which state or territory programs may apply.

Every field is optional. Nothing sensitive is needed.

A first enquiry needs a name, a way to reach you and roughly where you are. Consumption figures, roof photos and equipment details simply sharpen the response — send them if and when you are comfortable. A quote request never requires electricity account numbers, passwords or payment details, and no legitimate business needs your banking credentials to prepare one.

Coming from the estimator?

Your inputs and the modelled results are carried into the form automatically — adjust anything that looks off. It also helps to say what you thought of the numbers: too optimistic, too conservative, or matching your own experience of the bills.

What happens next

  1. We read it properly

    Your enquiry is reviewed against your postcode, property type and stated goal — not dropped into an automatic sequence.

  2. A first response with real questions

    Expect a reply that either answers your question directly or asks for the one or two details needed to answer it well.

  3. An assessment, then a design

    If it looks like a fit, we arrange a proper assessment of consumption, roof and switchboard before proposing a system.

How your details are handled

No automated enquiry inbox or public email address is configured yet. Nothing is transmitted anywhere unless you choose to copy your details.

We do not use tracking pixels or third-party analytics scripts on this site. Read the privacy page for the full description.
